questions.knowledge_point: Cases When a Square’s Side Is Mapped to a Parabola
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=u(u+v),\,y=\frac{2u}{v+1}.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{1}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{1}.$

For the side ${S}_{1},$ we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u(u+v),\,\frac{2u}{v+1}) \\  & =(u(u+0),\,\frac{2u}{0+1}) \\  & =({u}^{2},\,2u).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{1}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x={u}^{2},\,y=2u,\,0\le u\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)={t}^{2},\,y(t)=2t,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
x={(\frac{y}{2})}^{2}\,⇒\,{y}^{2}=4x
$$

which is a right-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(0,0).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{1}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(0,0)\to (0(0+0),\,\frac{2(0)}{0+1})=(0,0) \\  & T:(1,0)\to (1(1+0),\,\frac{2(1)}{0+1})=(1,2)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{1}$ is an arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(1,2).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/4fc3c209e83fc1d6b4c9258cdb739fb0a73db797791cf8fcca2e51a7592d54f8.png)

choices.value: An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(1,2).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(2,1)$ to $(1,0).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from  $(1,0)$ to $(2,1).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(1,2).$
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(1,2)$ to $(0,0).$

answer_fields.correct_value: An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(1,2).$

questions.knowledge_point: Finding the Image of a Square
questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/5f91cc8b30f9b764021cd84c374a328c7ffb1287a9f0dc6a211a3fadfac2fdbd.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1}
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x={u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,y=u.
$$

Find the image of $Δ$ under the action of $T.$ 

*Hint: You may assume that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$*
questions.worked_solution:
We're told that $T$ has no critical points in the interior of $Δ.$ So, to map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we transform each side of $Δ$ separately:

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{1},$ where we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{0}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2},\,u), & 0\le u\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a right-opening parabola traversed from the point $(0,0)$ to the point $(1,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{2}.$ Here, we have $u=1$ and $0\le v\le 1.$ Substituting $u=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({1}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,1) &  \\  & =(1+{v}^{2},\,1), & 0\le v\le 1.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a horizontal line segment traversed from the point $(1,1)$ to the point $(2,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{3}.$ Here, we have $v=1$ and $1\ge u\ge 0.$ Substituting $v=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{1}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+1,\,u), & 1\ge u\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

This is a right-opening parabola traversed from the point $(2,1)$ to the point $(1,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

- Consider the image of the side ${S}_{4}.$ Here, we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) &  \\  & =({u}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,u) &  \\  & =({0}^{2}+{v}^{2},\,0) &  \\  & =({v}^{2},\,0), & 1\ge v\ge 0.\end{aligned}
$$

 
This is a horizontal line segment traversed from the point $(1,0)$ to the point $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

Drawing the images of the sides of our square, we obtain the following image of $Δ:$

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ and its **directed** boundary $∂Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, where $Δ$ is given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=v-u,\,y={v}^{3}+u.
$$

The image of the side ${S}_{1}$ under the action of $T$ is a **directed** line segment. Find the endpoints of this segment, stated in the order that they are traversed.
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{1}.$

For the side ${S}_{1},$ we have $v=0$ and $0\le u\le 1.$ Substituting $v=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(v-u,\,{v}^{3}+u) \\  & =(0-u,\,{0}^{3}+u) \\  & =(-u,u).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{1}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=-u,\,y=u,\,0\le u\le 1.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=-t,\,y(t)=t,\,0\le t\le 1.
$$

This is a line segment with endpoints $(0,0)$ and $(-1,1)$ in the $xy$-plane.

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=2v(u-1),\,y=\frac{1}{2}v(4-u).
$$

The image of the side ${S}_{4}$ under the action of $T$ is a **directed** line segment. Find the endpoints of this segment, stated in the order that they are traversed.
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{4}.$

For the side ${S}_{4},$ we have $u=0$ and $1\ge v\ge 0.$ Substituting $u=0$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(2v(u-1),\,\frac{1}{2}v(4-u)) \\  & =(2v(0-1),\,\frac{1}{2}v(4-0)) \\  & =(-2v,2v).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{4}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=-2v,\,y=2v,\,1\ge v\ge 0.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=-2t,\,y(t)=2t,\,1\ge t\ge 0.
$$

This is a line segment with endpoints $(-2,2)$ and $(0,0)$ in the $xy$-plane.

questions.problem:
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/33e48fa5bdbb034bcf489e038ccf80fc5f67baabeccacc1b7abd741183ebf05d.png)

Consider the square region $Δ$ in the $uv$-plane, given by

$$
Δ={(u,v)\,:\,0\le u\le 1,\,0\le v\le 1},
$$

and the transformation $T,$ given by

$$
T:(u,v)\to (x(u,v),y(u,v)),
$$

where 

$$
x=u+v-2,\,y={u}^{2}-{v}^{2}.
$$

Which of the following is the image of the side ${S}_{3}$ under the action of $T?$
questions.worked_solution:
To map the entire region $Δ$ onto the $xy$-plane, we consider the transformation of each side. However, in this case, we consider only the side ${S}_{3}.$

For the side ${S}_{3},$ we have $v=1$ and $1\ge u\ge 0.$ Substituting $v=1$ into our transformation equations, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}(x,y) & =T(u,v) \\  & =(u+v-2,\,{u}^{2}-{v}^{2}) \\  & =(u+1-2,\,{u}^{2}-{1}^{2}) \\  & =(u-1,\,{u}^{2}-1).\end{aligned}
$$

So, the image of ${S}_{3}$ can be parametrized by

$$
x=u-1,\,y={u}^{2}-1,\,1\ge u\ge 0.
$$

 

Writing this in the usual notation, we have

$$
x(t)=t-1,\,y(t)={t}^{2}-1,\,1\ge t\ge 0.
$$

These are parametric equations of a parabolic arc. Notice that if we eliminate $t$ from the equations, we get

$$
y={(x+1)}^{2}-1
$$

which is an upward-opening parabola whose vertex is at $(-1,-1).$

Moreover, the endpoints of ${S}_{3}$ are mapped to the $xy$-plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned} & T:(1,1)\to (1+1-2,\,{1}^{2}-{1}^{2})=(0,0) \\  & T:(0,1)\to (0+1-2,\,{0}^{2}-{1}^{2})=(-1,-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the image of ${S}_{3}$ is an arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(-1,-1).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/multivariable/14063756/assets/b139c5b531191bc8aafbb14ad261989ef374503c63f54a567e695e287d4359be.png)

choices.value: An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(-1,0)$ to $(0,1).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(-1,-1)$ to $(0,0).$
An arc of a right-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,1)$ to $(-1,0).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(-1,-1)$ to $(1,1).$
An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(-1,-1).$

answer_fields.correct_value: An arc of an upward-opening parabola, traversed from $(0,0)$ to $(-1,-1).$
